$comment: Whether a host runs a manifest's linkLogin, and every rule it breaks, worded the same on both hosts: `lint` refuses the manifest with these, and a television, which runs no lint, reads the capability as absent and so runs the plugin signed out with no yonto.session. test/link-login.test.js walks it through src/link-login.js and LinkLoginsRecordTest through LinkLogins.kt.

cases.why: a service a host signs in to, on a plugin that cannot reach its account

refusals: linkLogin names example.test, which is not a service a host signs in to: plex.tv (contracts/link-logins.json)
allowedHosts entry plex.tv reaches plex.tv, where plex.tv's account is: only Yonto talks to it

cases.why: and through a wildcard, the discovery's host included
refusals: allowedHosts entry *.plex.tv reaches plex.tv, where plex.tv's account is: only Yonto talks to it

cases.why: a wildcard over the whole suffix admits it
refusals: allowedHosts entry *.tv reaches plex.tv, where plex.tv's account is: only Yonto talks to it

cases.why: a host below the account's domain it never asks is the account's too
refusals: allowedHosts entry www.plex.tv reaches plex.tv, where plex.tv's account is: only Yonto talks to it

cases.why: and one written in another case, or with a port
refusals: allowedHosts entry Clients.Plex.TV:443 reaches plex.tv, where plex.tv's account is: only Yonto talks to it

cases.why: a name that only ends like the domain is not below it

refusals: a linkLogin cannot stand beside hostsFromConfig, since nothing bounds where its requests go
a linkLogin cannot stand beside runsFetchedCode, since nothing bounds what code runs beside the session
a linkLogin cannot stand beside handles: a catalog is never offered a sign-in
a linkLogin cannot stand beside a cookieLogin: two host-held credentials on one source need a merge rule
a linkLogin cannot stand beside a browserCheck: two host-held credentials on one source need a merge rule
